tags.note: Re-audited 2026-08-24: prior claim that Felipe Cabeza 'discovered and moored most of Providencia's dive sites' could not be re-confirmed by any source (checked felipedivingshop.com/story/ directly) and has been removed as unsupported; only that the site is named for him and he founded Felipe Diving Center in 2003 is confirmed (2 sources). New: a submerged 'Christ Under the Waters' statue at ~24m, now fallen, is confirmed by both Pelecanus and The Dive Shop Old Providence.

Re-audited 2026-08-24: The Dive Shop Old Providence (local operator) explains the name -- large stingrays here are often mistaken for manta rays; no confirmed manta ray sightings at this site. Depth corrected from a placeholder 20m to the operator's stated 5-12m range (using 12m as representative maximum); the prior 20m figure could not be traced to any source. Citation to myscubadivinggearguide.com removed -- that page does not mention this site anywhere (re-checked directly).

Re-audited 2026-08-24: citation to myscubadivinggearguide.com removed -- that page does not mention Nick's Place, Spiral, or Sponge Valley anywhere (re-checked directly). Site type/depth confirmed by 2 sources (Just Gotta Dive's 'NX', The Dive Shop Old Providence) as a wall with a crack/platform dropping to 40m+, Advanced. CONFLICT: Pelecanus describes 'Nick's Place' as a shallow reef (15-30m), low difficulty, with only 'sponges and reef fish' -- a materially different site character. Kept as wall/40m/Advanced per the 2-source majority and flagged the discrepancy in the markdown rather than silently resolving it.

Re-audited 2026-08-24: citations to pelecanus.com.co and myscubadivinggearguide.com removed -- neither page mentions 'The Pinnacle' or 'The Peak' anywhere (re-checked both directly). Only SeaCrush ('The Peak') independently confirms this site, describing dramatic pinnacles to ~35m, Advanced, with pelagics/manta rays. Could not find a 2nd or 3rd independent source despite additional English and Spanish searches. Left validated=true per QA policy (do not flip based on source count alone) but this site does NOT meet the 3-source bar as of this audit -- flagged for future research.

Re-audited 2026-08-24: all 3 sources re-confirmed directly (Just Gotta Dive, Joe's Scuba Shack, Pelecanus). Pelecanus additionally notes bottom time at the deepest section is typically limited to a few minutes given the depth -- single-source detail, included as a hedged operator note rather than a firm fact.

Re-audited 2026-08-24: the previously stated '500 square metres' cay size was incorrect -- Wikipedia gives the island's area as 0.02 km2 (~20,000 sq m), 40x larger than previously stated; corrected. Citation to myscubadivinggearguide.com dropped (that page only lists 'Crab Caye' as a generic island activity, no dive-specific content) and replaced with wikipedia.org. TripAdvisor content (site itself returns 403 to direct fetch) re-confirmed via multiple indexed review excerpts: triggerfish, needlefish, 'thousands of baby fish' under the wooden pier, and an occasional small shark.

RENAMED from 'Blue Diamond' on 2026-08-24 deep-QA pass. Re-audit found overwhelming, consistent evidence across 8+ independent sources (PADI, Zentacle, TripAdvisor, dive.site, sanandresislandpreview.com, YouTube, sanandresisla.travel) that the wreck named 'Blue Diamond' / 'Barco Hundido' is located exclusively at San Andres island (~12.535N, -81.736W), ~90km from these coordinates -- NOT at Providencia. The prior citation of myscubadivinggearguide.com as evidence of a Providencia-based 'Blue Diamond' does not hold up: that page was re-checked directly and does not contain the string 'Blue Diamond' anywhere. Meanwhile, 4 independent sources (The Dive Shop Old Providence, Just Gotta Dive, Waterpixels, Agenda del Mar) consistently describe 'El Planchon' as THE documented WWII-era wreck at Providencia, at these approximate coordinates, and no source describes any second/different Providencia wreck. Renamed accordingly and re-validated. UNRESOLVED WRECK-HISTORY CONFLICTS (kept as explicit conflicts in the markdown, not resolved by guessing): (1) depth reported between 15m (Just Gotta Dive, Agenda del Mar) and 18-24m (The Dive Shop Old Providence); (2) vessel origin -- most sources describe it as a Colombian-flagged ship that resupplied German U-boats in WWII, but one source (Roads and Rivers) calls it simply a 'German tanker'; (3) the claim that the crew scuttled it themselves as the war ended appears in only one weakly-sourced account and is flagged as unconfirmed, not stated as fact. No length or tonnage is given -- a PADI-listed 'El Planchon' with a 30m/12-ton profile was checked and found to be a DIFFERENT wreck at Fuerte Island, Cordoba (9.363N, -76.176W), not Providencia; those dimensions are NOT applied here to avoid conflating the two vessels. Sinking date not independently confirmed. Penetration is not permitted per every source consulted.

Re-audited 2026-08-24: 'peacock flounder' and 'yellow-spotted stingray' claims removed -- neither could be re-confirmed at this specific site by any source on re-check (only generic 'stingrays' confirmed, via The Dive Shop Old Providence). Pillar coral re-confirmed by 2 independent sources (Scuba Diving Magazine, colombia-travels.com) in addition to the operator description. Added: bluestriped/French grunts and puffer fish specifically confirmed at this site (Waterpixels); occasional bottlenose dolphins (single-source, The Dive Shop Old Providence, hedged); bioluminescent ostracods on night dives (2 sources: Scuba Diving Magazine, colombia-travels.com).

Re-audited 2026-08-24: The Dive Shop Old Providence (local operator, direct fetch) describes 'Convento' as a platform with extensive sandy areas and a cliff wall, 16-40m, Intermediate, with lobsters, crabs, snappers, stingrays, and gray reef sharks -- reclassified from 'reef' to 'wall' and depth/difficulty updated on this basis (this is a genuine dive-specific source, unlike the prior generic tourism attribution). Still only 2 independent domains found (this operator + the original Felipe Diving Facebook confirmation) despite additional English and Spanish searches -- left validated=false pending a 3rd independent source.

Re-audited 2026-08-24: the ScubaBoard thread previously cited (threads/providencia-questions-our-first-real-diving-experience.316728/) was re-read in full and does NOT mention Table Rock anywhere -- citation removed as unsupported. Depth, caves, silversides, and nurse sharks remain confirmed by 2 independent sources (Joe's Scuba Shack, Deep Blue Hotel).
